newsitem.title: USA: Terminix settles Florida pest complaints.
newsitem.headline: Terminix settles Florida pest complaints.

text.p: Pest-control group Terminix International will re-inspect as many as 50,000 Florida homes as part of a deal settling consumer complaints of failed service, the Florida attorney general said Wednesday.

Terminix, a unit of ServiceMaster L.P., will also pay $200,000 to cover the cost of a state investigation and the agreement could cost the Terminix millions of dollars, Attorney General Bob Butterworth said in a joint news release with Florida's Agriculture Department.

"Our joint investigation revealed that in many instances, Terminix failed to fully treat properties for subterranean termites, despite its promise to lay down a complete protective barrier against the destructive insects," Crawford said.

Terminix said in a news release that the agreement, which calls for re-inspection of many termite-control jobs carried out over the past four years, includes no costs material to its parent's financial performance and included no admissions of fault on the company's part.
Floridians covered by the agreement are eligible for re-inspection of ground eradication jobs and may cancel their Terminex projects or obtain a retreatment.
